title: Geometrically integral flat finite-presentation algebra is projective over the base
statement: Let $R\to B$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Assume that for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and every field extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, the ring $B\otimes_R K$ is an integral domain; residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field]. Then $B$ is a projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], equivalently a direct summand of a free $R$-module.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $C=B\otimes_R k$. For a field extension $K/k$ the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives mutually inverse maps $(B\otimes_R k)\otimes_k K\longleftrightarrow B\otimes_R K$, given by $(b\otimes a)\otimes t\mapsto b\otimes at$ and $b\otimes t\mapsto(b\otimes1)\otimes t$. They respect multiplication and units on pure tensors, which generate the tensor products. Thus $C\otimes_k K$ is an integral domain for every $K/k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the base change $(\operatorname{Spec}C)_K=\operatorname{Spec}C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_kK)$, and by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] the spectrum of an integral domain is an integral scheme. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is geometrically integral over $k$ in the sense of [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], which is the fibre hypothesis of the theorem used in Step 2.

proof.text: Apply the existing theorem [lem-trf-local-fibres-integral-projective] to the given ring map $R\to B$. Its finite-presentation and flatness hypotheses are assumptions of this item, and its geometric-integrality hypothesis for every fibre ring is Step 1. Its conclusion gives that $B$ is a projective $R$-module. The cited node already states Tag 05FT in full, so this application reuses that existing theorem rather than creating a second node for its Noetherian reduction.

By [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], projectivity of $B$ is equivalent to the existence of a free $R$-module $F=\bigoplus_{i\in I}R$ and $R$-linear maps $i:B\to F$, $s:F\to B$ with $s\circ i=\mathrm{id}_B$. This is the asserted direct-summand formulation.
